Claude Code defaults effort to medium on these models, high on most others. Nothing signals the change.

With no output_config.effort the API applies medium on these models; every other model that supports effort defaults to high, Claude Opus 5 included, so a request that omits effort runs one level lower on Opus 5.5. GET /v1/models lists the effort levels, not the default.

tool_choice any or tool returns 400 on every request. Send tool_choice auto with strict tools or structured outputs, and say in the prompt when to call the tool. On other models forced tool use works with adaptive thinking, and the response then starts with the tool call with no thinking block.

Thinking is on with no thinking field. disabled at xhigh or max returns 400. /v1/models now declares thinking.types.disabled but not the effort limit. With thinking off, the model can skip a tool call it needs when JSON output is also requested. A per-message output_config.effort that differs from the level in effect returns 400 while thinking is off.

Thinking is on with no thinking field. disabled at xhigh or max returns 400, checked on each request. With thinking disabled the model can occasionally emit tool calls as plain text or internal XML tags in its visible output.

A request whose final turn is a prefilled assistant message returns 400, whether or not thinking is on. Put continuations in the user message, or use structured outputs to shape the reply. Earlier models refuse prefill only while thinking is on.

From API version 2026-10-21, a request carrying temperature, top_p or top_k at any value returns 400 on every model. On earlier API versions, Claude Opus 4.7 and later, Sonnet 5 and later, Haiku 5.5, Fable and Mythos models return 400 for any non-default value, thinking or not; their top_p default is 0.99, so top_p 1 returns 400, and so does sending temperature and top_p together even at their defaults. The 4.6, 4.5 and Haiku 4.5 models restrict them only while thinking is on (top_p 0.95 to 1). Omit the three parameters.

Effort levels keep their names but are recalibrated against Claude Sonnet 5: a level does not produce the same amount of thinking. Anthropic's starting points: medium for well-specified agentic work (high for harder or longer tasks), medium or low for chat and latency-sensitive work.

thinking.type "disabled" returns a 400 on this model; to run without up-front thinking send {"type": "between_tools"} (progress updates between tool calls still come back as thinking blocks). between_tools is refused (400) at effort xhigh and max, accepts no display, budget_tokens or block_binding, and fixes the effort for the whole conversation (a per-message output_config.effort that differs returns 400). With no thinking field the model thinks (adaptive). Since 2026-10-16 GET /v1/models declares between_tools supported and disabled unsupported, but neither the effort limit nor the fixed effort.

disabled returns 400. between_tools turns off up-front thinking only: progress updates between tool calls still come back as thinking blocks; without tools the response is text only. Thinking is on with no thinking field.

Thinking blocks from these models work only in the account that produced them or an account linked to it. Sent by another account, the blocks are dropped before the model sees them and the request still succeeds: the model answers without that reasoning. Blocks from earlier models are not affected.
Thinking cannot be turned off: disabled and between_tools return 400. Lower the effort to think less. Claude Mythos Preview also accepts enabled with budget_tokens.

Each thinking block is signed over the conversation before it. For accounts created on or after 2026-08-31 00:00 UTC, replaying a block after any edit to system, tools or earlier messages returns 400 (older accounts only when thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior is set). Keep requests append-only; change instructions or tools with mid-conversation system messages and tool_addition/tool_removal blocks. prefix_mismatch_behavior drop_block is a stopgap that raises output tokens, and on Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 it works only with adaptive thinking.
disabled turns thinking off at any effort. With no thinking field, Claude Sonnet 5 thinks; the 4.x models do not.

Other names are aliases: minimal maps to low, medium and xhigh to high, ultra to max.

deepseek-flash now serves DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017; name, request and price unchanged. DeepSeek reports higher benchmarks with shorter outputs and faster runs: a measurement taken before 2026-10-17 is of the previous model. The page does not say whether deepseek-v4-flash, still served by V4.1-Flash, follows.

In thinking mode temperature, presence_penalty and frequency_penalty are accepted without error and have no effect. top_p differs by model: deepseek-flash applies it only in thinking mode, clamped to 0.95-1.0, and fixes it at 1.0 without thinking; deepseek-v4-pro ignores it in thinking mode (fixed at 0.95 when tools are present, else 1.0) and applies it without thinking.

Thinking is on with no thinking field. OpenAI and Anthropic formats: {"thinking": {"type": "disabled"}} (with the OpenAI SDK, inside extra_body). Responses API format: reasoning.effort "none" instead.

PDF files are read by models with vision capabilities: the API sends the model both the extracted text and an image of each page. Chat Completions takes a PDF as a file content part; models without Chat Completions (Pro, Codex) take it through the Responses API as input_file. The model pages do not list PDF among input modalities, and their file_uploads feature is present on some models and absent on others without saying what it means for PDF.
